$comment: The loop engine's own rules (issue #1195, owner decision 2026-09-22). @clossys/controller (packages/controller/src/loop/*) is the one pure implementation; every staffed repository installs it as an exact dev dependency. Roles declare data -- their own clossys/<role>/loop.json -- and the engine runs them. This contract, and the code it mirrors, is the deterministic-mechanics half of the split the owner recorded on issue #1187: packages own definition, judgment, and deterministic mechanics; the coding agent does generative work and live external changes.

stageMeaning.judge: Compare with the setpoint, then choose. The human approval gate sits here.
stageMeaning.verify: Measure the effect of this action.
stageMeaning.learn: Adapt the setpoint, model, or rule -- or escalate, handing the problem to the enclosing loop when this one cannot close it. Renamed from learnOrEscalate by issue #1194: escalation was always one of learn's own outcomes, not a second stage.

invocation.rule: One invocation runs one iteration and stops at the approval gate inside judge. No skill in this repository is named bare `loop` -- Claude Code's own built-in /loop is for recurring runs.

perCapability.$comment: State and condition are independent: a capability can be approved and stale at the same time. See ./lifecycle.json for both vocabularies.

state.statusSectionsRule: Exactly these five sections, in this order. The Advisor lane writes Advisor's own STATUS.md in parallel (issue #1187's plan) with the same five sections; the renderer (packages/controller/src/loop/status.ts's renderStatusDocument) is deliberately generic over its caller's section bodies so the engine can take over rendering Advisor's STATUS.md later without a shape change.
state.runHistory: Git history is the run history. There are no per-run files.

triggers.change: the role itself (a package upgrade, a new check)
an outcome (a metric missed at review)

blockers.rule: A blocked capability rests with exactly one next action (who, how, by when) and escalates past its due date. Other capabilities keep running -- state is per-capability, so one capability's blocker never touches another's.

staleness.rule: Every artifact records fingerprints of the inputs it was built from, so staleness is a deterministic comparison (packages/controller/src/loop/staleness.ts). Changes propagate only through dependents: a capability with no declared dependency on a changed input is never marked affected by it.
staleness.planBinding: A plan is bound to the assessment it came from; if that assessment changes, the plan is re-proposed as a diff and never executed as written.

rules.create: Own folder only (clossys/<role>/), by pull request.
rules.update: Own folder only, by pull request. A human's edit is detected by fingerprint and merged, never overwritten.
rules.move: Fixes every reference in the same pull request.
rules.supersede: Append-only proof gets a new entry and is never deleted.
rules.retire: Only files the role's own manifest lists, and only after checking dependents.

resume: An interrupted run resumes from disk and any open pull request: a capability's own recorded stage is read back exactly, never re-derived or guessed. A regression after merge triggers the work item's rollback -- an outcome signal that reaches learn, whose decision may be to act again as a rollback.

ownership.rule: One pure implementation in @clossys/controller (the loop, artifacts, blockers, staleness, and status-rendering modules). Roles declare data -- clossys/<role>/loop.json and, indirectly, their own manifest outputs and needs/feeds (docs/contracts/package-framework.json) -- and the engine runs them. Controller is installed in every staffed repository as an exact dev dependency named by the plan.
ownership.changeProcedure: A change to the stages, triggers, blocker kinds, or artifact-operation rules above is exactly one pull request: it bumps this file's own schemaVersion and packages/controller/src/loop/* in the same change.
